root.meaning: of a brother or sister; genuine
root.note: From germen ‘shoot, sprout’. It has nothing to do with Germania or the Germans.

history: Latin had a perfectly good word for brother: frāter. But Romans also said frāter germānus, a true brother with the same father and mother. In Hispanic speech germānus, ‘genuine’, took over the job, and it became ermano, then hermano. Frāter retired to the Church, giving Spanish fray and fraile, ‘monk’. The old meaning of germānus still appears in primo hermano, ‘first cousin’, a true, full cousin. Despite the look, it has nothing to do with Germans: the word is from germen, ‘sprout’. The h is only spelling: Old Spanish wrote ermano, and modern Spanish doesn't pronounce it.
historyEinfach: Hermano means ‘brother’. In Latin, the word for brother was frāter. A real brother, with the same parents, was frāter germānus. In Spain, people kept only germānus. It became hermano. The old word frāter lives on in fray, ‘monk’. And hermano does not come from ‘German’. The Spanish h is silent.

elsewhere.text: English germane, ‘relevant’, comes from the same Latin word as hermano.
Italian kept the frāter line that Spanish gave up: only Hispanic speech chose germānus.
French frère belongs to the same frāter line.
